title: Black Swan
synopsis: You've earned the lead in Swan Lake — the pure White Swan you were born to dance, and the dark Black Swan you'll have to become. The mirror is starting to disagree with you. How far will you go to be perfect?

nodes.text: The director, Thomas, paces the studio. 'I need a Swan Queen who can be both — innocence and seduction, light and dark.' The other dancers watch you like wolves in legwarmers. The part should be yours. It almost is.

choices.text: Dance only the pure, perfect White Swan
choices.consequence: Control is your gift and your prison. You choose to dance only the pure, perfect White Swan. By The Mother, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

choices.text: Try to find the wild Black Swan in yourself
choices.consequence: You can't fake what you've never let yourself feel. You choose to try to find the wild Black Swan in yourself. By Thomas's Test, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: At home your mother has already laid out your dinner, your nightgown, your future. 'My sweet girl,' she says, smoothing your hair, locking the door behind her smile. The room is pink and small and yours and not yours.

choices.text: Thank her and stay the good daughter
choices.consequence: Obedience is a soft cage with a key you can't find. You commit to thank her and stay the good daughter. It carries you into Lily while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

choices.text: Push back, just a little
choices.consequence: The first crack lets in light and rot both. You choose to push back, just a little. By The First Scratch, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: Thomas corners you after rehearsal. 'Perfection is not just control,' he murmurs, too close. 'It's also letting go.' His method blurs the line between teaching and trespass, and he knows exactly how off-balance he's put you.

choices.text: Let him provoke the dark in you
choices.consequence: The role demands a door you're afraid to open. You choose to let him provoke the dark in you. By Lily, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

choices.text: Hold your boundary and your control
choices.consequence: Saying no costs you the part — maybe. You hold your boundary and your control. The way toward The First Scratch opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: A new dancer, Lily, moves like she was born without fear — sloppy, alive, magnetic. She could be your friend. She could be your understudy. She could be after your role. With her, you can never quite tell.

choices.text: Befriend Lily and learn her looseness
choices.consequence: Open your guard and see what walks in. You choose to befriend Lily and learn her looseness. By The Night Out, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

choices.text: Watch Lily as a rival to be beaten
choices.consequence: Suspicion sharpens you and isolates you. You commit to watch Lily as a rival to be beaten. It carries you into The Reflection Lies while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: You find marks on your shoulder you don't remember making. A rash, your mother says. A sign, the mirror seems to whisper. You begin checking your reflection for a face that isn't quite doing what you're doing.

choices.text: Tell yourself it's just exhaustion
choices.consequence: Denial is a stage you can dance on for a while. You tell yourself it's just exhaustion. The way toward The Night Out opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

choices.text: Start watching the mirror back
choices.consequence: What you look for, you find. You start watching the mirror back. The way toward The Reflection Lies opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: Lily drags you out — drinks, music, a pill she promises will 'help you let go.' For one night you are loose and laughing and free, dancing in a dark club instead of a bright studio. You wake unsure what was real.

choices.text: Embrace the wildness it unlocked
choices.consequence: The Black Swan stirs and stretches her wings. You commit to embrace the wildness it unlocked. It carries you into Becoming the Black Swan while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

choices.text: Recoil in shame the next morning
choices.consequence: The good girl claws her way back to the surface. You recoil in shame the next morning. The way toward Cracking opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: In the long studio mirrors your reflection turns its head a half-beat late. It smiles when you don't. Once, you'd swear it kept dancing after you stopped. You tell no one. Telling someone would make it true.

choices.text: Confront the mirror directly
choices.consequence: Stare into it and it stares back, smiling. You commit to confront the mirror directly. It carries you into Becoming the Black Swan while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

choices.text: Avoid mirrors and push through
choices.consequence: You can't dance ballet without mirrors. You'll learn that. You choose to avoid mirrors and push through. By Cracking, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: In rehearsal, finally, it happens — you stop counting, stop controlling, and let something hungry take the floor. Thomas weeps. The company stares. You have never felt so powerful or so unlike yourself. Choose “Chase that feeling no matter the cost” and The Rival, Closer comes into view; choose “Be frightened by what came out of you” and the road bends toward The Help You Reach For.

choices.text: Chase that feeling no matter the cost
choices.consequence: Power like this is a debt you'll be billed for. You chase that feeling no matter the cost. The way toward The Rival, Closer opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

choices.text: Be frightened by what came out of you
choices.consequence: Fear is the last sane voice in the room. You commit to be frightened by what came out of you. It carries you into The Help You Reach For while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: Your toenails, your skin, your sleep — your body is keeping a tally your mind won't. You hide the worst of it under makeup and tights. Your mother hovers; Thomas pushes; the mirror waits. Something has to give, and it's you.

choices.text: Hide it all and dance anyway
choices.consequence: The show is a god that eats its dancers. You choose to hide it all and dance anyway. By The Rival, Closer, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

choices.text: Reach out for help, once
choices.consequence: A hand extended, even shaking, is still a hand. You commit to reach out for help, once. It carries you into The Help You Reach For while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: Lily is made your alternate — your safety net, or your replacement, depending on how you look at her. You find her in your dressing room, or you imagine you do. You can no longer tell the difference, and it's starting to feel like a knife.

choices.text: Accuse Lily of trying to steal the role
choices.consequence: Paranoia and truth have begun to share a face. You commit to accuse Lily of trying to steal the role. It carries you into Opening Night Approaches while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

choices.text: Decide you must simply be better than her
choices.consequence: Turn the fear into fuel and burn yourself for warmth. You decide you must simply be better than her. The way toward The Mirror Shatters opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: Maybe a doctor, maybe a friend, maybe just one honest sentence to your mother. The help is real and the relief is real — but opening night is in three days, and the part is your whole identity. Can you be saved and still be the Swan Queen?

choices.text: Take the help and risk losing the role
choices.consequence: Your life is worth more than a curtain call. Probably. You commit to take the help and risk losing the role. It carries you into Stepping Back while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

choices.text: Refuse the lifeline to protect the part
choices.consequence: The role has its hooks in deep now. You refuse the lifeline to protect the part. The way toward The Mirror Shatters opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: The hallucinations sharpen — feathers under your skin, your legs bending the wrong way, your reflection living its own life. You are dancing better than ever and unraveling faster than ever, on the exact same thread.

choices.text: Lean fully into the transformation
choices.consequence: Maybe madness and perfection are the same place. You lean fully into the transformation. The way toward The Black Swan's Dance opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

choices.text: Fight to hold onto yourself
choices.consequence: There may still be a 'you' left to save. You commit to fight to hold onto yourself. It carries you into The White Swan's Truth while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: Backstage on opening night, the confrontation comes — with Lily, with your reflection, with the dark thing wearing your face. Glass breaks. You feel a sharp, terrible relief, and a spreading warmth you don't look at.

choices.text: Believe you've defeated your rival
choices.consequence: The mind protects itself with terrible stories. You commit to believe you've defeated your rival. It carries you into The Black Swan's Dance while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

choices.text: Begin to suspect there was no rival at all
choices.consequence: The most dangerous person in the room was always the one in the mirror. You commit to begin to suspect there was no rival at all. It carries you into The White Swan's Truth while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: You walk out of the theater the night before the premiere. It feels like dying and like being born. Your understudy goes on; the reviews are fine; the world does not end. You are not the Swan Queen. You are, perhaps, alive.

choices.text: Grieve the role but keep your life
choices.consequence: Some losses are the shape of survival. You commit to grieve the role but keep your life. It carries you into The Dancer Who Walked Away while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

choices.text: Wonder forever if you could have been perfect
choices.consequence: The road not danced haunts the longest. You choose to wonder forever if you could have been perfect. By The Understudy's Triumph, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: You take the stage and you are no longer dancing the Black Swan — you are her. The audience disappears. You spin and spin and feel wings, real wings, and the most exquisite freedom of your life. Nothing has ever been this perfect.

choices.text: Finish the dance no matter what
choices.consequence: Perfection has a price and you've already paid it. You finish the dance no matter what. The way toward Curtain Call opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

choices.text: Come back to yourself before the final act
choices.consequence: The fall toward earth is the most human thing. You come back to yourself before the final act. The way toward The White Swan's Truth opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: In the wings, between acts, the fog clears for one terrible lucid moment. You understand what you've done to your body, your mind, your reflection. The wound is yours. The rival was yours. The choice, now, is also yours.

choices.text: Go back out and dance the ending anyway
choices.consequence: Finish beautifully and let go of everything. You go back out and dance the ending anyway. The way toward Between the Acts opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

choices.text: Call for help and step out of the story
choices.consequence: Choosing to live is the bravest exit there is. You commit to call for help and step out of the story. It carries you into The Quiet Wings while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: The bows. The roses. Thomas climbing onto the stage to kiss the back of your hand. You smile through everything because smiling is the next step, and the next step is the only step that matters. Something warm is spreading at your side and you do not look down.

choices.text: Let the applause carry you
choices.consequence: Joy and dying can rhyme, briefly. You let the applause carry you. The way toward Perfect opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

choices.text: Finally, finally, look down
choices.consequence: Reality is the last person to arrive at the party. You choose to finally, finally, look down. By Looking Down, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: You go back out and finish — and somewhere in the second-to-last lift you feel your body decide it is done bargaining with you. The audience does not know. They will not, for one more aria.

choices.text: Dance the last act with everything left
choices.consequence: Some final notes are the best ones. You commit to dance the last act with everything left. It carries you into Perfect while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

choices.text: Drop the role mid-leap and walk off
choices.consequence: Refusing the script is its own kind of grace. You choose to drop the role mid-leap and walk off. By The Quiet Wings, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: Backstage is suddenly louder than the stage — Thomas raging, Lily wide-eyed, your mother crying without sound. You make the smallest, hardest gesture of your career: you sit down and ask for an ambulance. “Tell them the whole truth about everything” draws you toward Imperfect, Alive; “Just hold your knees and breathe” leaves The Dancer Who Walked Away waiting on the other side.

choices.text: Tell them the whole truth about everything
choices.consequence: Honesty in the wings is the harder choreography. You choose to tell them the whole truth about everything. By Imperfect, Alive, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

choices.text: Just hold your knees and breathe
choices.consequence: Sometimes survival is wordless. You just hold your knees and breathe. The way toward The Dancer Who Walked Away opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: Red on white. Of course. You laugh, almost — at yourself, at the cost of perfection, at how obvious it was. There is one more breath in which you can decide what this night meant. Choose “Decide it meant perfection” and Perfect comes into view; choose “Decide it meant a warning, in time” and the road bends toward Imperfect, Alive.

choices.text: Decide it meant perfection
choices.consequence: Some stories end on a high note, on purpose. You commit to decide it meant perfection. It carries you into Perfect while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

choices.text: Decide it meant a warning, in time
choices.consequence: Even at the curtain you can rewrite an ending. You decide it meant a warning, in time. The way toward Imperfect, Alive opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: The final note. The white feathers. The leap. The audience erupts and Thomas calls your name and you smile, because you felt it — you were, for one impossible night, perfect. The warmth at your side spreads. 'I was perfect,' you whisper, and mean it, as the lights go soft.

You stop the show. There are gasps and then ambulances and then, weeks later, a quiet room and a real recovery. You will dance again or you won't, but you will be there to choose. Perfection nearly killed you. Imperfection, it turns out, is where you get to live.

You left ballet, or ballet left you, and for a long time it felt like amputation. Then one ordinary morning you dance in your kitchen for no audience at all and feel, faintly, joy — the kind that doesn't bleed. You are nobody's Swan Queen. You are nobody's victim either.

Lily dances the Swan Queen and the reviews call her a revelation. You watch from the back of the house, healthy and hollow, applauding a perfection that might have been yours. You'll never know. That not-knowing is the role you dance for the rest of your life.
